q: Build a DataFrame of three students with a name, a city and a mark, and print it.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Anita", "Rohit", "Meena"],
    "city": ["Chennai", "Pune", "Delhi"],
    "mark": [72, 85, 64]
})
print(df)
out:
name     city  mark
0  Anita  Chennai    72
1  Rohit     Pune    85
2  Meena    Delhi    64

q: Print the first two rows using iloc, and the salary of the row labelled 2 using at.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df.iloc[0:2])
print(df.at[2, "salary"])
out:
name  dept  salary  exp
0  Rahul    HR   47764    4
1  Priya  Tech   62990    7
51200

q: Print everyone earning more than 50,000, and count how many that is.
code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],
    "dept":   ["HR", "Tech", "Sales", "Tech", "HR"],
    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})

print(df[df["salary"] > 50000])
print((df["salary"] > 50000).sum())
out:
name   dept  salary  exp
1  Priya   Tech   62990    7
2   Amit  Sales   51200    3
3  Kavya   Tech   58300    6
3

q: Print how many people are in each department, and the average salary of the table.
code:

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name":   ["Rahul", "Priya", "Amit", "Kavya", "Arjun"],

    "salary": [47764, 62990, 51200, 58300, 45100],
    "exp":    [4, 7, 3, 6, 2]
})
